title: Disinformation Network Connects with Media, Politicians, and 560,000 ‘Bot’ and ‘Troll’ Accounts
author: Darylh Rodríguez
content:
_This article by[Darylh Rodríguez](https://contralinea.com.mx/author/darylh/)
originally appeared in the [August 14, 2026 edition of
Contralínea](https://contralinea.com.mx/interno/semana/red-de-desinformacion-
conecta-con-medios-politicos-y-560-mil-cuentas-de-bots-y-trolls/), an
independent Mexican investigative journalism magazine._

Behind millions of posts that appear simultaneously on social media there may
not be a crowd voicing opinions, but rather a structure designed to produce
that impression. The Presidency's Legal Counsel maintains that this is what
happens with a digital amplification network that would have been used to
produce narratives against President Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo and the so-called
Fourth Transformation. Its head, Luisa María Alcalde Luján, asserted that this
network is not organic, since it involves media outlets, commentators,
political figures, attack accounts, and **more than 560,000 bot and troll
accounts**. After this information was made public, communicators named in it
and NGOs described the data as the government's "fascist lists," while the
president and the legal counsel denied that these are "blacklists": it is an
analysis of the digital ecosystem of artificial trend amplification, they
stated.

![Diagram of the first layer of the digital amplification
network](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/08/2026-08-14-disinformation-network-02-layer1.jpg)Photo:
Presidencia

An alleged digital amplification network made up of opposition political
figures, public figures, anonymous users, and a total of 560,520 accounts
would be operating against President Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo and the movement
of the so-called Fourth Transformation, with the purpose of spreading false
narratives and thereby altering public perception, by coordinately replicating
negative messages and systematic campaigns with certain hashtags and social
trends. This, according to an analysis presented by the head of the Legal
Counsel of the Presidency of the Republic, Luisa María Alcalde Luján.

The assessment points to a "digital amplification ecosystem," made up of four
layers in which different types of accounts and users participate with certain
differentiated functions. Among them are media outlet accounts, commentators,
profiles related to political figures, anonymous accounts or accounts
identified as trolls, and, finally, a broad amplification ring composed of
more than 560,000 accounts that together would have generated **around 22.7
million posts during the seven months analyzed, from January 1 to August 8,
2026**.

According to the information presented during the Right of Reply press
conference on August 12 at the National Palace, the first layer would be made
up of 54 accounts of media outlets and political commentators. A group that
constitutes, according to Alcalde Luján, the point of origin of a large part
of the messages that later circulate through the other levels. Among the names
mentioned are Atypical TV, Bibiana Belsasso, Adela Micha, Ciro Gómez Leyva,
Dolia Estévez, Javier Negre, ADN40, Azteca Noticias, El Universal, Joaquín
López-Dóriga, La Derecha Diario, Carlos Loret de Mola, Aristegui Noticias,
Denise Dresser, and Javier Alatorre, among others.

In this way, the first-stage accounts would have accumulated a total of
282,866 posts during the analyzed period. Their role, according to the federal
interpretation, would consist of generating or legitimizing content through
tailored news, columns, comments, supposed investigations, and the
dissemination of opinions that would later be picked up by other users on
social media. "Their importance is that they originate the message," Luisa
María Alcalde stated in the same press conference.

![Presentation slide on the media and commentator
accounts](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/08/2026-08-14-disinformation-network-03-fascist-
lists.jpg)Photo: Presidencia

After this information was made public, communicators named as part of this
digital disinformation structure and NGOs—such as the Miguel Agustín Pro
Juárez Center—described the data as the government's **" fascist lists,"**
while President Sheinbaum Pardo and the legal counsel **denied that these are
"blacklists."** In a video shared on social media, attorney Luisa María
Alcalde asserted that it is an analysis of the digital ecosystem of artificial
trend amplification and of those who appear in it.

For her part, President Sheinbaum Pardo denied that what Alcalde presented is
a registry comparable to fascist regimes. In her morning press conference on
August 14, she indicated that a scientific analysis was carried out and that
paid bot networks were identified.

![President Claudia Sheinbaum at her morning press
conference](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/08/2026-08-14-disinformation-
network-04-sheinbaum.jpg)Photo: Presidencia

"They're already saying it's 'Sheinbaum's list'; I invite you to watch the
Right of Reply press conference by Luisa María again […]. What Luisa says is:
'a piece of news comes from one account and from there an entire mechanism is
set off against a political position, against a project, against the
president.' She showed how social media works today; she never said: 'this is
the list of who knows what.' No." She added that under her government "the
greatest freedom of expression in history" is exercised. And she asked: "Who
is being censored? Who? No one."

![Presentation on the coordinated amplification
mechanism](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/08/2026-08-14-disinformation-
network-05-freedom.jpg)Photo: Presidencia

> Who is being censored? Who? No one.
>
> President Claudia Sheinbaum

## Second Layer: Politicization

The second layer would be made up of 32 accounts related to political figures,
to which more than 67,000 posts were attributed. At this level, Alcalde Luján
explained, the messages are picked up, endorsed, and given a political slant
before moving on to the following stages of circulation. "They mainly pick up,
endorse, and politicize the information they gather from layer one."

Among the politicians and public figures mentioned by the legal counsel are
Alejandro Moreno, Felipe Calderón, Javier Lozano, Maru Campos, Rubén Moreira,
Jorge Romero, Lilly Téllez, Margarita Zavala, Ricardo Anaya, Vicente Fox,
Claudio X. González, Marko Cortés, Ricardo Salinas Pliego, Kenia López,
Lorenzo Córdova, Xóchitl Gálvez, Damián Zepeda, Laura Ballestero, Luisa
Gutiérrez, Lía Limón, Mauricio Tabe, Santiago Taboada, Annia Gómez, Enrique de
la Madrid, Gabriel Quadri, Jorge Triana, Federico Döring, and Guadalupe Acosta
Naranjo.

The third layer would be made up of 34 accounts identified as "attack"
accounts or trolls, which would accumulate more than 200,000 posts. "They are
in charge of repackaging and distributing the message," Luisa María Alcalde
stated. In other words, the function at this stage consists of taking up
messages generated at the previous levels, reformulating them, and adding
confrontational content, before distributing them among a larger number of
users.

In this group, the Morena member showed as examples the accounts Melissa Bely,
La Abuela García, José Díaz, Jorge García Orozco, and Don Metralleta; which,
according to the data presented, register certain particularly intense
activity patterns, with practically continuous posting during much of the day.

The case of Melissa Bely was used as one of the main examples. Luisa María
Alcalde noted that this account would have a share equivalent to **around 30
percent of the daily movement** identified within this level of the network,
and that a high proportion of its content would be directed against President
Claudia Sheinbaum and the so-called Fourth Transformation.

> We used Melissa Bely as an example because, as we saw on the digital map,
> this is the account that today concentrates what amounts to 30 percent of
> the daily movement of the entire ring of 560,000 accounts, the one with the
> most interaction with the bots. It starts at 6:00 a.m., 36 posts a day; that
> is, practically all of its posts—96 percent of its posts—are dedicated to
> attacking the Fourth Transformation, to attacking the president of Mexico,
> with aggressive language, using nicknames, phrases like "scandal" or "boom"
> to grab attention and to try to generate outrage.

Regarding the fourth layer, Alcalde explained that by far the largest number
of accounts resides in it. This is the so-called "amplification ring," which
is made up of 560,520 accounts that would be accumulating around 22 million
posts, with the aim of repeating and multiplying the messages that come from
the previous levels.

It is precisely at this point that the scale of the structure takes on greater
relevance, the official maintained. However, she clarified that these 560,000
accounts are profiles that do not correspond to people, but rather form part
of an amplification pattern. With this, Alcalde explained that the hypothesis
is based on the fact that within that universe there are behaviors compatible
with automated accounts, although the existence of a high posting frequency
does not by itself constitute definitive proof that an account is a bot.

Based on the above, the counsel said that the activity of these accounts can
generate a perception effect; that is, a narrative that is initially placed by
a media outlet, commentator, or political figure—aligned with the
opposition—can be picked up by attack accounts and subsequently reproduced
thousands or millions of times. In this way, any conversation can take on an
apparently larger dimension through the coordinated, or also automated,
repetition of certain content.

"So, the first thing to understand in order to break down this network is that
we have four phases, four layers, and each one has a function and each one has
specific accounts," she stated at the Right of Reply press conference held on
August 12.

Moreover, among the narratives identified by the Mexican government are
accusations of an alleged "narco-government," the so-called "fiscal huachicol"
(fuel-tax fraud), claims about an alleged "authoritarian regime," as well as
content related to pressures or "foreign intervention." Concepts, the official
asserted, used recurrently, since they are also adapted to different events in
the national political situation.

According to the information presented in the same press conference, the
described mechanism consists of a narrative that can begin as some kind of
information, opinion, or political claim; it is later picked up by other
actors, transformed into attack content, and finally turned into mass posts.
This results in an amplification circuit in which it becomes difficult to
distinguish the origin of a message from the thousands of times it is
subsequently reproduced.

Another of the elements addressed by the official are the so-called behavior
patterns of these accounts, which post with a frequency incompatible with the
usual behavior of a user, while others remain active throughout the day. Also
identified were name changes, the repeated use of certain hashtags, the mass
production of memes and videos, and a high concentration of messages against
President Sheinbaum.

In light of this information, Contralínea asked Luisa María Alcalde directly
about the possibility of following the money trail behind this structure,
considering the magnitude of the identified universe, the volume of posts, as
well as the activity sustained over seven months. This, in the context that
maintaining a digital operation of this scale can involve different types of
resources, both for account management, content production, and the hiring of
digital services, as well as for automation tools, technological
infrastructure, and advertising.

However, Alcalde responded that, for now, the government's objective is to
expose the phenomenon and allow the population to identify this type of
mechanism, rather than to present an investigation into its financing. While
she acknowledged that identifying the resources and those who might eventually
be behind these structures would be a different path, she maintained that, at
this stage, the aim is only to generate tools so that people do not confuse an
artificially amplified trend with a widespread social conversation.

"Well, that in any case is up to the institutions, to the INE itself. The INE
always audits the resources of the political parties; it is part of its powers
and responsibilities: that the use of these resources go specifically toward
what is permitted. Financing a scheme of this nature would not be permitted,
much less with the intent to disinform. But, well, that is the exclusive
authority of the Electoral Institute."

And she added that the government's intention is to expose the phenomenon and
generate a space for joint reflection. "Because it is very important that we
all know that when we talk about bots, it's not that one says: 'no, no, don't
worry, there are no people behind them.' No. It is proven; we can show you how
these accounts work, and that they have been increasing."

![Presentation on the amplification ring of more than 560,000
accounts](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/08/2026-08-14-disinformation-network-06-bots.jpg)Photo:
Presidencia

## Audience Rights in the Face of Disinformation

On another matter, this weekly asked the legal counsel about audience rights.
In the same press conference, Contralínea asked whether the federal government
or the Legal Counsel itself had considered expanding obligations not only for
print media, but also for digital media and accounts operating on social
media, in order to clearly differentiate information, opinion, and
advertising. With this, the question was raised of whether audiences could
have mechanisms to file complaints when disinformation is spread, particularly
in a context where journalistic content, political opinions, advertising, and
artificially generated messages can circulate within the same platforms.

In response, Luisa María Alcalde noted that expanding the guidelines to other
types of media has not been contemplated. "Let's say, there isn't even that
intention for now." The official explained that the government is currently
focused on establishing the guidelines derived from a law passed in 2025, and
denied that there is, for the moment, any intention to expand those
obligations in the terms proposed.

The legal counsel maintained that the discussion about audience rights has
generated various interpretations, and asserted that some of the "false
narratives" that circulated around the guidelines had already been clarified,
including through statements from the industry itself. In this way, the
official drew a distinction between print and audiovisual media. In the case
of newspapers, she noted, it is easier to identify the difference between
advertising, informational content, and opinion, since traditionally there are
differentiated spaces for each of them.
